entries.subject: Hui et al. (2026) Hubble WFC3 nucleus photometry
entries.finding: Effective radius 1.3 ± 0.2 km at assumed V-band geometric albedo 0.04 (H 17.1 ± 0.4) and a sky-plane axis ratio of at least 2:1 from brightness changes of at least 0.8 mag. The display is a prolate ellipsoid at the minimum 2:1 ratio whose geometric-mean cross-section equals π × (1.3 km)².

entries.subject: Jewitt et al. (2025) July 2025 Hubble nucleus limit
entries.finding: Before perihelion the coma hid the nucleus; the fit only limited the radius to at most 2.8 km. The 2026 post-perihelion detection supersedes it for size.
entries.revisitWhen: The 2026 detection is revised or retracted.

entries.subject: Artist impressions and coma photographs as surface textures
entries.finding: Hubble, JWST and spacecraft images show an unresolved nucleus inside its coma; none maps the surface.
entries.revisitWhen: Resolved imaging of the nucleus exists.

entries.subject: Published shape model, pole or rotation period
entries.finding: Only a lower limit of about 1 hour on the period and the 2:1 axis-ratio limit are published. The display pole, meridian and spin phase are arbitrary.
entries.revisitWhen: A lightcurve inversion, pole solution or rotation period is published.

entries.subject: JPL Horizons fixed-epoch trajectory
entries.finding: Horizons 3I (C/2025 N1) elements and independent vectors at the 2026-09-03 scene epoch: eccentricity 6.12 at 10.88 au. Two-body propagation differs from Horizons by 964 km and 873 km 30 days either side.

entries.subject: Measured colour as a whole-body Color lens
entries.finding: Published colours (spectral slopes of about 18 to 23% per 100 nm across the visible) were measured on the dust coma. The Hubble nucleus photometry used one filter, so no nucleus colour exists to paint on the body.
entries.revisitWhen: A nucleus colour is published; the disc-integrated colour route can then add a Color lens.
